signals.title: USD — FOMC Decision + Yield Curve Regime
signals.text: The FOMC announces its latest interest rate decision today, July 29, with markets broadly expecting a hold at 3.75%. Despite the expected hold, the 2s10s yield curve sits in a bull steepener regime at +29.4bp, typically signaling recession pricing and cross-asset stress. US 10Y yields have retreated to 4.604% while the DXY holds at 101.33, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (101.06/100.43/99.14). COT speculative positioning shows a light net short of -1,948, suggesting the market is not positioned for a hawkish surprise. Any hawkish dissent or guidance keeping rates elevated for longer introduces upside risk for the DXY toward the next psychological resistance. Risk: A dovish pivot or clear signal of upcoming cuts accelerates the bull steepener and undercuts DXY support at the SMA20.

signals.title: AUD/USD — CPI Miss + ESI Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6946, testing its SMA20 support at 0.6965 following softer-than-expected Australia CPI data. This data miss aligns with a strong negative Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of -21.2, suggesting a persistent trend of Australian data underperforming expectations. While the RBA holds a nominal carry advantage at 4.35% vs the Fed's 3.75% (-60bp AUD premium), the real policy rate remains deeply accommodative at -1.15% due to high inflation expectations. Speculative positioning is currently net long +20,521, creating a liquidation risk as the soft CPI data tempers hike odds. A sustained break below the SMA20 reopens the SMA200 level at 0.6906. RBA holds at 4.35%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Skew + Vol
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 163.53, supported by a significant +275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential despite the BoJ's hiking stance. However, the options market shows rising caution with a 25d Risk Reversal of -1.49, indicating a moderate put skew as traders pay for protection against JPY strength. This is coupled with an elevated Vol Risk Premium (VRP) of +3.4%, as 1M ATM IV at 7.2% remains well above the realized HV30 of 3.8%. COT data shows specs are heavily net short JPY (-114,030), leaving the pair vulnerable to a sharp unwind if the next BoJ meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on July 31 delivers a hawkish surprise. Price remains technically bullish, holding above the SMA20 at 162.57. Risk: BoJ holds without hawkish guidance, allowing the carry trade to extend toward 165.00.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning + Vol Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD is trading at 1.3305, currently positioned below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3377/1.3365/1.3398). The options market is pricing a high degree of uncertainty ahead of the July 30 BoE meeting, with a significant VRP of +4.5% (IV 11.0% vs HV30 6.5%). Speculative positioning remains net long +33,812 (66.3% long), which contrasts with a mildly accommodative real policy rate of -0.13%. BoE holds at 3.75%. Retail sentiment at 65% long aligns with the institutional long, increasing the risk of a synchronized washout. Risk: BoE signals a surprise hike, triggering a sharp move back through the SMA cluster.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Correlation Break + Positioning
signals.text: USD/CAD is trading at 1.4097, showing a significant correlation break against WTI Oil (corr -0.915 vs norm -0.021, z = -1.55σ). While WTI oil rose 3.57% to $82.1, the expected CAD strength has been muted by a heavy COT speculative net short in CAD of -99,823 (only 18.8% long). The pair is currently holding below its SMA20 at 1.4122 but remains supported by a +150bp carry advantage in favor of the USD. Retail sentiment is 70% short, fading the recent move, which typically serves as a contrarian signal for further USD/CAD upside. Watch for the correlation to normalize or for oil price exhaustion to trigger a fresh bid in the pair. Risk: Oil prices break above $85, forcing a CAD short-covering rally that overrides the carry disadvantage.
